messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw two nodes in us-west-2 report recurrent ECC/Xid bursts overnight. They flapped healthy/unhealthy 3 times each in ~6h. We had an aggressive drain that requeued several long-running Slurm jobs, expensive churn. Can we design a soft-drain/hysteresis flow to avoid noisy evictions?

emily: +1. We should smooth the signal and require repeated confirmation before cordon. Also separate actions: mark node as \"soft-quarantine\" first (no new pods/sched) then escalate to cordon+drain if persistent.

raj: For Slurm vs k8s we need different behavior. Slurm jobs could be put into a drain partition or set to NO_NEW_JOB, but not necessarily requeue instantly. For k8s, annotate and cordon, but delay drain so GPU jobs can finish small batches.

kai: Proposal sketch: 3-stage pipeline — 1) signal ingest and dedupe, 2) soft-quarantine (node taint + annotation), 3) hard-cordon+drain if signal persists beyond hysteresis window. Default params: require 3 ECC/Xid spikes within 5m window OR sustained ECC rate > threshold for 10m. Backoff before re-enabling: 30m.

sam: That sounds good. Specifics we should discuss: metric math, tolerances to avoid false positives, max concurrent nodes in hard-cordon to protect pool capacity. Also need observability hooks.

emily: Metric smoothing idea: use an exponential moving count over events: score_t = alpha * event + (1-alpha) * score_{t-1}. Trigger when score > 2.5 (tuned per gpu model). This avoids single-burst triggers.

raj: For capacity guardrails: do not escalate to hard-cordon if pool has < 10% spare capacity or if Dedicated pool is below SLA threshold. Instead mark for manual review and notify oncall. Also add a per-region concurrent limit (e.g., 2 nodes/region) to avoid correlated drains.

kai: Implementation notes for ops-bot: we can implement automations with a safe playbook. Example commands we would run when going from soft->hard: 
```
kubectl annotate node $NODE gpu.health=soft-quarantine --overwrite
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=critical' --grace-period=120
```
For Slurm: `scontrol update NodeName=$NODE State=DRAIN Reason=\"gpu-health\"` then let scheduler finish short jobs, requeue long ones as last resort.

ops-bot: Automation check: detected node i-0abcdef (us-west-2) hit ECC spike threshold. Applied annotation gpu.health=soft-quarantine at 2026-03-11T02:15Z. Will re-evaluate in 5m.

sam: We should also tag the node `gpu:flaky=true` and add it to a review queue in the console so hardware team can inspect before replacement. Avoid immediate replace unless FATAL.

emily: Observability: emit these events to metrics: `gpu_ecc_spike_count`, `gpu_health_score`, `node_soft_quarantine_count`. Dashboards: per-model histograms, per-region counts, and a small runbook link on the panel. Alerting: page only when a node moves to hard-cordon AND concurrent_cordoned > 0.

raj: For SLURM sensitivity: add job-age-aware decisions. If the node is running >24h jobs, prefer `NO_NEW_JOB` and schedule replacement during maintenance window to avoid huge requeues.

kai: Edge cases: 1) noisy telemetry (duplicates) — dedupe by device UUID + 1s window; 2) GPU ECC count resets on driver reload — treat resets as negative evidence and require fresh spikes post-reset; 3) network partition — ensure bot can't cordon nodes it can't reach (double-check kube-apiserver connectivity).

sam: Cost/ops tradeoff note: each accidental requeue costs ~hours of wasted GPU time. Let's be conservative with hard actions. Default: soft-quarantine after 1 confirmed spike cluster-wide, hard-cordon only after 3 confirmations within 10m AND capacity guardrails pass.

emily: I'll draft a config YAML for tuning. Early version: 
```
health_policy:
  ecc:
    spike_count: 3
    window_sec: 600
  hysteresis:
    confirm_backoff_min: 30
    reevaluate_sec: 300
  capacity_guardrails:
    min_free_percent: 10
    max_concurrent_cordon_per_region: 2
  slurm:
    prefer_no_new_job_if_job_age_sec: 86400
```

kai: Nice. Ops-bot should also add `runbook_url` to the node annotation and post a short summary in #eng-infra when it hard-cordons.

ops-bot: FYI — when a node is soft-quarantined the autoscaler will deprioritize scheduling but will not scale up automatically. If a hard-cordon happens and free capacity < min_free_percent, autoscaler may trigger scale-up depending on pool config.

sam: Next actions: emily to open PR with the initial policy + config defaults, kai to prototype ops-bot run, raj to add Slurm integration notes in runbook. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 9:30 PT to ratify thresholds. Thanks. :thumbsup:

emily: will do.

raj: noted, adding to runbook.

kai: prototyping now — will post link to branch.
